explanationIssues: In the phase conversion the formula uses degrees and the result uses radians: 「−cosθ = sin(θ−90°) を用いると i = 50 sin(1000t−π/2)」. Here θ = 1000t is in radians, so the formula should read 「−cosθ = sin(θ−π/2)」. If a degree statement is kept, it should only appear afterwards as 「π/2 = 90° 遅れ」.
figureIssues: figureDescription says only 「矢印付きで電流 i の向きを示し」 and never says the i arrow points right. It also never says that the tip of the left-pointing v arrow marks the positive (higher-potential) left terminal. The directions of i and v decide whether the element is a coil or a capacitor. Someone reading only the text therefore cannot check the polarity, even though the explanation depends on it. Suggested fix: add something like 「上辺の i の矢印は右向き（素子へ流入）」 and 「v の矢印は左向きで、矢印の先端側（左端子）が高電位」.
verifiedEvidence: Question text matches the original: the element is a coil L or a capacitor C, v = 500 sin(1000t) [V], i = −50 cos(1000t) [A]. The only changes are line breaks and punctuation.
Choices (1)–(5) match the original: C=10 nF, C=100 nF, C=10 μF, L=10 mH, L=100 mH.
The official answer table (令和6年度上期 理論 問15(a)) gives 4, the same as officialAnswer.

Polarity checked on the original figure. The i arrow on the top wire points right, into the element. The v arrow under the source points left, so the left terminal is positive. Current leaves the source's positive terminal, goes up the left wire and enters the element from the left. The element therefore follows the passive sign convention, and v and i can be compared as given.
−cos(1000t) = sin(1000t − π/2), so i = 50 sin(1000t − π/2). The current lags the voltage by 90°, which means the element is an inductor.
|Z| = 500/50 = 10 Ω = ωL, so L = 10/1000 = 0.01 H = 10 mH. This gives choice (4), matching the official answer.

Recomputed each wrong choice. (1) X_C = 1/(1000×10×10⁻⁹) = 100 kΩ. (2) 1/(1000×100×10⁻⁹) = 10 kΩ. (3) 1/(1000×10×10⁻⁶) = 100 Ω. (5) ωL = 1000×0.1 = 100 Ω. All four figures in choiceExplanations are correct. Choices (1)–(3) are also wrong because a capacitor's current would lead, which contradicts the 90° lag.
The public figure matches the original in connections, arrow directions and every label (i, 回路素子, the ~ source, v). No labels are missing or mixed up.
Question text matches the original, including the proviso: (1/2)Li² for an inductance and (1/2)Cv² for a capacitance.
The official answer table (令和6年度上期 理論 問15(b)) gives 3, the same as officialAnswer.
With L = 0.01 H from (a) and current amplitude Im = 50 A, W_max = (1/2)×0.01×50² = 12.5 J. This gives choice (3), matching the official answer.

Recomputed each wrong choice. (1) Reaching 2.5 J needs L = 2 mH at Im = 50 A, or I = √500 ≈ 22.4 A at L = 10 mH. (2) Using the rms value, Irms² = 1250, gives (1/2)×0.01×1250 = 6.25. (4) Dropping the 1/2 factor gives 0.01×2500 = 25. (5) Using L = 0.1 H gives (1/2)×0.1×2500 = 125. All the stated reasons are correct.
